Summary  
The paper argues that neuromorphic hardware (especially self-assembled nanowire networks) could remove present scaling limits of conventional GPUs, but that these devices raise new AI-safety concerns: (1) the emergence of misaligned AGI on energy-efficient, easily scalable hardware, (2) the opacity of spike-based, in-memory computations, and (3) low-cost self-assembly that could accelerate uncontrolled proliferation.  It proposes broadening current software-centric safety work to include hardware-level interpretability and plasticity-control research and recommends funding existing neuromorphic capability researchers to tackle these topics.  The knowledge fabric below captures all causal-interventional pathways from the three top-level risks to the concrete interventions implied or explicitly recommended in the text.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[78]  
The paper is mainly conceptual and policy-oriented, so several implementation and validation links required moderate inference; however, all core reasoning chains are represented and interconnected.  JSON was validated for key consistency (node names ↔ edge references, required attributes present, no illegal risk-intervention edges).  

Inference strategy justification  
Where the authors implied but did not spell out interventions (e.g., embedding diagnostics, safety-constrained training loops) I used moderate domain inference and marked edge confidence 2.  Policy recommendations (grant programmes) were taken directly.  

Extraction completeness explanation  
The fabric contains 23 nodes (≈18/5 k words) and 24 edges.  Every claim that functions as a step in any reasoning chain is a distinct node; framework names are decomposed; all nodes participate in at least one path and categories follow the mandated order.  

Key limitations  
• Few hard empirical results exist, so validation evidence nodes rely on single studies (edges confidence ≤ 3).  
• Governance-level interventions are high-level; detailed mechanisms (e.g., grant administration) are not in the source.  
• Some causal directions (e.g., “mitigated_by”) are debatable given the conceptual nature of arguments.
